parts.instructions: This paper has 50 multiple choice questions (1 to 50). Each question has 4 choices. Choose ONE best answer and blacken its letter on the separate answer sheet.

questions.stem: An instrument used to measure the mass of an object is:
explanation_steps: A beam balance compares an object with known masses. It measures mass.
A metre stick measures length, a stop watch measures time, and a newton meter (spring balance) measures force or weight. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 8)
questions.explain_simple: We measure mass with a beam balance.
tips: Mass → balance. Weight (force) → newton meter.

similar_questions.stem: Which instrument measures time?
explanation_steps: A stop watch measures time.

questions.stem: Organisms which feed on dead plants and animals are called:
explanation_steps: Decomposers (for example bacteria and fungi) break down dead plants and animals to get energy.
Carnivores eat animals, herbivores eat plants, and producers make their own food. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 127)
questions.explain_simple: Decomposers feed on dead plants and animals.
tips: Decomposers return nutrients to the soil.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is a decomposer?
explanation_steps: Fungi break down dead things, so they are decomposers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-renewable natural resource?
explanation_steps: Oil (petroleum) is a fossil fuel. It took millions of years to form and it cannot be replaced once used.
Air and water are renewed by nature, and soil can be kept fertile. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 62)
questions.explain_simple: Oil cannot be made again quickly, so it is non-renewable.
tips: Fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas) are non-renewable.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a renewable source of energy?
explanation_steps: Wind will not run out, so it is renewable.

questions.stem: A scientific guess made to solve a problem is:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'A hypothesis is a scientific guess.'
An experiment tests the hypothesis; a conclusion comes at the end. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: A scientific guess is called a hypothesis.
tips: Scientific method: observe → question → hypothesis → experiment → conclusion.

similar_questions.stem: In the scientific method, what do we do to test a hypothesis?
explanation_steps: We do an experiment to see if the hypothesis is right or wrong.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not correct about the nucleus of an atom?

options.A: it is fixed at the center of an atom
options.B: it is fixed in the atomic shell
options.C: it is positively charged part of an atom
options.D: it is made up of protons and neutrons

explanation_steps: The nucleus is in the centre of the atom. It has protons and neutrons, so it is positively charged.
The shells (energy levels) are outside the nucleus. Electrons move in the shells, not the nucleus.
So 'it is fixed in the atomic shell' is not correct. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 75)
questions.explain_simple: The nucleus is in the centre. The shells around it hold electrons, not the nucleus.
tips: Centre: nucleus (protons + neutrons). Shells: electrons.

similar_questions.stem: Where are the electrons of an atom found?

options.B: in the shells around the nucleus

explanation_steps: Electrons move around the nucleus in shells.

questions.stem: The type of joint that allows nodding and turning movement is called:
explanation_steps: The pivot joint is between the head and the vertebrae (neck). It lets the head nod and turn.
A hinge joint moves only in one direction (knee, elbow); a fixed joint does not move; a gliding joint allows only slight movement. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 32)
questions.explain_simple: The pivot joint in the neck lets the head turn and nod.
tips: Pivot = turning (neck). Hinge = like a door (knee, elbow).

similar_questions.stem: Which type of joint is found at the knee?
explanation_steps: The knee moves like a door hinge, so it is a hinge joint.

questions.stem: Matter that has a definite volume but has no definite shape is:
explanation_steps: A liquid has a definite volume but takes the shape of its container.
A solid has a definite shape and volume; a gas (and steam) has neither. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 50)
questions.explain_simple: A liquid keeps its volume but changes its shape.
tips: Solid: fixed shape + volume. Liquid: fixed volume only. Gas: nothing fixed.

similar_questions.stem: Which one is a solid?
explanation_steps: A stone has a definite shape and a definite volume.

questions.stem: Which of the following cells is not important for sexual reproduction?
explanation_steps: In sexual reproduction a male sex cell joins a female sex cell.
Sperm cells and pollen grains carry male sex cells; egg cells are female sex cells.
A nerve cell is a body cell. It carries messages, not genes for a new organism. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 204)
questions.explain_simple: A nerve cell is a body cell. It is not a sex cell.
tips: Sex cells: sperm, egg, pollen (male), ovule (female).

similar_questions.stem: In flowering plants, the male sex cells are found in the
explanation_steps: Pollen grains carry the male sex cells of a plant.

questions.stem: Vessels that carry blood from body organs back to the heart are:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'The veins carry blood from the body organs back towards the heart.'
Arteries (and small arterioles) carry blood away from the heart. Capillaries are the tiny vessels between them. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Veins bring blood back to the heart.
tips: Arteries → Away from the heart. Veins → back to the heart.

similar_questions.stem: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
explanation_steps: Arteries carry blood away from the heart.

questions.stem: The amount of heat energy needed to raise the temperature of one gram of water by 1 °C is called:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'A calorie is the amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one gram of water by 1 °C.'
Kelvin is a temperature scale, not an amount of heat. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: The heat to warm 1 g of water by 1 °C is one calorie.
tips: 1 calorie = heat for 1 g of water, 1 °C. The SI unit of heat is the joule.

similar_questions.stem: The SI unit of heat energy is the
explanation_steps: The textbook says the joule (J) is the SI unit of heat.

questions.stem: In figure 1, two forces are applied on an object. Then, which of the following is true?
questions.image_alt: Figure 1: a box. On the left an arrow F₁ = 10 N pushes it to the right; on the right an arrow F₂ = 4 N pushes it to the left.

options.C: the object moves to the right
options.D: the object moves to the left

explanation_steps: F₁ = 10 N pushes to the right. F₂ = 4 N pushes to the left.
The forces are in opposite directions, so net force = 10 N − 4 N = 6 N to the right.
The forces are unbalanced, so the object moves in the direction of the bigger force: to the right. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 49)
questions.explain_simple: 10 N to the right is bigger than 4 N to the left. The box moves right.
tips: Opposite forces: subtract. The object moves toward the bigger force.

similar_questions.stem: A box is pushed with 8 N to the left and 8 N to the right. What happens?
explanation_steps: Equal and opposite forces are balanced. The net force is 0.

questions.stem: At puberty, the release of an egg from the ovary of a female is:
explanation_steps: The release of an egg (ovum) from the ovary is called ovulation.
Fertilization is the joining of sperm and egg; menstruation is the monthly bleeding; menopause is when ovulation stops. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 25)
questions.explain_simple: When the ovary releases an egg, it is ovulation.
tips: Ovum = egg → ovulation = releasing an egg.

similar_questions.stem: The stage when a woman stops ovulation is called
explanation_steps: The textbook says menopause is when a female stops ovulation.

questions.stem: A farm tool used for splitting a wood is:
explanation_steps: An axe has a heavy sharp blade (a wedge). It is used for cutting and splitting wood.
A hoe digs soil, a sickle harvests crops and cuts grass, and shears cut soft branches and leaves. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 108; Science Grade 7, p. 17)
questions.explain_simple: We split wood with an axe.
tips: Axe → wood. Sickle → crops, grass. Hoe → soil.

similar_questions.stem: Which tool is used for harvesting crops like wheat?
explanation_steps: A sickle is used for harvesting crops and cutting grass.

questions.stem: A machine has a mechanical advantage of 6. The effort required to lift a load of 240 N is:
explanation_steps: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort, so effort = load ÷ M.A.
Effort = 240 N ÷ 6 = 40 N. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 5)
questions.explain_simple: Effort = load ÷ MA = 240 ÷ 6 = 40 N.
tips: M.A = L ÷ E, so E = L ÷ M.A.

similar_questions.stem: A lever lifts a load of 300 N with an effort of 100 N. Its mechanical advantage is

questions.stem: The trachea:

options.A: conducts air from throat to the stomach
options.B: conducts food from throat to the lungs
options.C: conducts blood from throat to the heart
options.D: conducts air from throat to the lungs

explanation_steps: The trachea (windpipe) is part of the respiratory system.
Air goes from the pharynx (throat) into the trachea and then to the lungs.
Food goes to the stomach through the oesophagus, not the trachea. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 12)
questions.explain_simple: The trachea carries air from the throat to the lungs.
tips: Trachea = windpipe (air). Oesophagus = food pipe.

similar_questions.stem: Tiny air sacs in the lungs where gases are exchanged are called
explanation_steps: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the alveoli (air sacs).

questions.stem: The third energy level (M shell) of an atom can accommodate a maximum of:
explanation_steps: The maximum number of electrons in a shell is 2n², where n is the shell number.
First shell (K): 2. Second (L): 8. Third (M, n = 3): 2 × 3² = 18. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 76; Science Grade 8, p. 80)
questions.explain_simple: The third shell can hold up to 18 electrons.
tips: Maximum electrons: K = 2, L = 8, M = 18 (rule 2n²).

similar_questions.stem: The second shell (L shell) can hold a maximum of
explanation_steps: 2 × 2² = 8 electrons.

questions.stem: A car accelerates uniformly from a speed of 2 m/s to a speed of 14 m/s in 3 seconds. What is its acceleration?
explanation_steps: Acceleration = (final velocity − initial velocity) ÷ time.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 58)
questions.explain_simple: The speed grows by 12 m/s in 3 s. 12 ÷ 3 = 4 m/s².
tips: a = (v − u) ÷ t.

similar_questions.stem: A bicycle speeds up from 1 m/s to 9 m/s in 4 s. Its acceleration is

questions.stem: An example of acquired traits is:
explanation_steps: An acquired trait is gained during life. It is not passed on by genes.
A tattoo is made on the skin during life, so it is acquired.
Ear structure, nose structure and eye colour are inherited from parents. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 142)
questions.explain_simple: A tattoo is made after birth, so it is an acquired trait.
tips: Inherited = from parents' genes. Acquired = gained during life.

similar_questions.stem: Which is an inherited trait?
explanation_steps: Blood group comes from the genes of the parents.

questions.stem: How many atoms are there in Ca(OH)₂?
explanation_steps: Ca(OH)₂ has 1 calcium atom. The small 2 after the bracket doubles everything inside: 2 oxygen atoms and 2 hydrogen atoms.
Total = 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 atoms. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 86)
questions.explain_simple: 1 Ca + 2 O + 2 H = 5 atoms.
tips: A number after a bracket multiplies every atom inside the bracket.

similar_questions.stem: How many atoms are in one molecule of H₂O?
explanation_steps: 2 hydrogen atoms + 1 oxygen atom = 3 atoms.

questions.stem: Which pair represents nonmetal elements?
explanation_steps: Copper, zinc, gold and silver are metals.
Oxygen and carbon are both nonmetals. (In D, sulphur is a nonmetal but silver is a metal.) Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 37)
questions.explain_simple: Oxygen and carbon are both nonmetals.
tips: Common nonmetals: hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, carbon, sulphur.

similar_questions.stem: Which element is a metal?
explanation_steps: Iron is shiny, strong and conducts electricity. It is a metal.

questions.stem: Objects that are good reflectors and bad absorbers of heat are:
explanation_steps: Black surfaces absorb heat well; white (light, shiny) surfaces reflect heat.
Rough surfaces absorb heat well; smooth surfaces are bad absorbers.
So a white and smooth surface is the best reflector and worst absorber. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 115)
questions.explain_simple: White and smooth surfaces reflect heat and absorb little.
tips: Black + rough = good absorber. White + smooth = good reflector.

similar_questions.stem: Why do people in hot places often wear white clothes?
explanation_steps: White reflects the sun's heat, so the body stays cooler.

questions.stem: The reading of a Fahrenheit thermometer is 104 °F. This is equivalent to ______ °C.
explanation_steps: (textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 122)
questions.explain_simple: Take away 32 and multiply by 5/9: 104 °F = 40 °C.

similar_questions.stem: Convert 50 °F to °C.

questions.stem: The process of keeping constant internal environment in mammals is:
explanation_steps: Homeostasis is keeping the inside of the body (temperature, water, etc.) constant.
Homoeothermic and poikilothermic describe warm- and cold-blooded animals; appendicular is a part of the skeleton. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 34)
questions.explain_simple: Keeping the inside of the body steady is homeostasis.
tips: Homeo = same, stasis = staying.

similar_questions.stem: When we are hot, we sweat. This helps
explanation_steps: Sweating cools the body and keeps its temperature constant (homeostasis).

questions.stem: A type of satellite that receives radio signal messages from one location and transmits them to another location is:
explanation_steps: Communication satellites receive radio signals from one place and send them to another place.
They are used for telephone, radio and television. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 156)
questions.explain_simple: Satellites that pass on radio messages are communication satellites.
tips: Communication → messages. Weather → clouds and storms. Navigation → finding position.

similar_questions.stem: Which satellite helps to forecast rain and storms?
explanation_steps: Weather satellites watch clouds and storms.

questions.stem: Solid ice melts to liquid water at a temperature of:
explanation_steps: Ice melts (and water freezes) at 0 °C, which is 32 °F (not −32 °F).
100 °C = 212 °F is the boiling point of water. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 121)
questions.explain_simple: Ice melts at 0 °C.
tips: Water: freezes/melts at 0 °C (32 °F); boils at 100 °C (212 °F).

similar_questions.stem: Water boils at
explanation_steps: Pure water boils at 100 °C (212 °F).

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a magnetic substance?
explanation_steps: Magnetic substances are attracted by a magnet. Pins, paperclips and nails are made of iron or steel, so they are magnetic.
Wood is not attracted by a magnet. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 173)
questions.explain_simple: A magnet does not pull wood.
tips: Iron and steel things are magnetic. Wood, plastic, paper are not.

similar_questions.stem: Which object will a magnet attract?
explanation_steps: An iron nail is magnetic.

questions.stem: Identify the chemical symbol of potassium:
explanation_steps: The symbol of potassium is K. It comes from its Latin name, kalium.
P is phosphorus, Al is aluminium and Au is gold. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 85)
questions.explain_simple: Potassium's symbol is K.
tips: Latin symbols: Na (sodium), K (potassium), Fe (iron), Au (gold), Ag (silver).

similar_questions.stem: Fe is the symbol of
explanation_steps: Fe comes from the Latin name ferrum, which means iron.

questions.stem: Which of the following is common to boys and girls at puberty?
explanation_steps: At puberty, hair grows under the armpits and in the groin of both boys and girls.
Sperm production and penis growth happen only in boys. Breast growth happens in girls. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 25)
questions.explain_simple: Both boys and girls grow hair under the arms at puberty.
tips: Both: armpit and pubic hair, growth spurt. Boys only: sperm, deeper voice. Girls only: breasts, menstruation.

similar_questions.stem: Which change happens only in girls at puberty?
explanation_steps: Only girls start menstruation.

questions.stem: The tiniest blood vessels in the human circulatory system are called:
explanation_steps: Capillaries are the smallest (tiniest) blood vessels. They join arterioles to venules.
The vena cava is the biggest vein. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 19)
questions.explain_simple: Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels.
tips: Artery → arteriole → capillary (smallest) → venule → vein.

similar_questions.stem: Which is the largest vein in the body?
explanation_steps: The vena cava is the largest vein. It brings blood back to the heart.

questions.stem: In figure 2, the basic parts of a cell indicated as 1, 2 and 3 are:
questions.image_alt: Figure 2: a round grey cell with a black dot inside. Label 1 points to the outer edge, label 2 to the grey inside, label 3 to the black dot.

options.A: cell membrane, cytoplasm, and cell wall

explanation_steps: Part 1 is the thin outer edge of the cell: the cell membrane.
Part 2 is the grey jelly that fills the cell: the cytoplasm.
Part 3 is the dark round body in the middle: the nucleus. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 102)
questions.explain_simple: 1 = cell membrane, 2 = cytoplasm, 3 = nucleus.
tips: Basic parts of every cell: cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus.

similar_questions.stem: Which part controls all the activities of a cell?
explanation_steps: The nucleus is the control centre of the cell.

questions.stem: The components that form a fire triangle are:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Any fire needs three things: fuel, heat and air (oxygen).' This is the fire triangle.
If one of them is missing, the fire goes out. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Fire needs fuel, heat and oxygen.
tips: Remove one side of the triangle and the fire stops.

similar_questions.stem: Putting sand on a small fire stops it mainly because sand

options.B: stops oxygen from reaching the fire

explanation_steps: Sand covers the fire so oxygen cannot reach it.

questions.stem: Weight of an object is equal to:
explanation_steps: The textbook gives: weight = mass × gravity (W = m × g).
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Weight = mass × gravity.
tips: W = m × g, with g ≈ 10 N/kg on Earth.

similar_questions.stem: A bag has a mass of 5 kg. Take g = 10 N/kg. Its weight is

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: a compound cannot be separated into its elements by physical means
options.B: muddy water is an example of heterogeneous mixture
options.C: sugar dissolved in water is an example of homogeneous mixture
options.D: substances in a homogeneous mixture can be identified by seeing

explanation_steps: In a homogeneous mixture (like sugar water) the parts are mixed evenly. You cannot see them separately.
So D is wrong. A, B and C are all correct statements. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 44; Science Grade 7, p. 36)
questions.explain_simple: In a homogeneous mixture you cannot see the different parts. So D is wrong.
tips: Homogeneous = looks the same everywhere. Heterogeneous = you can see the parts.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a heterogeneous mixture?
explanation_steps: You can see the sand and the iron filings, so the mixture is heterogeneous.

questions.stem: If an object vibrates 100 times in one second, its frequency is:
explanation_steps: Frequency is the number of vibrations in one second. It is measured in hertz (Hz).
100 vibrations in one second = 100 Hz. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 204)
questions.explain_simple: 100 vibrations each second is 100 Hz.
tips: 1 Hz = 1 vibration per second.

similar_questions.stem: A string vibrates 600 times in 2 seconds. Its frequency is
explanation_steps: 600 ÷ 2 = 300 vibrations per second = 300 Hz.

questions.stem: A shadow of an object is formed, when the:

options.A: object blocks a beam of light
options.B: object transmits a beam of light
options.C: object partially transmits a beam of light
options.D: object partially blocks a beam of light

explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'A shadow is formed whenever an opaque object blocks a beam of light.'
Light travels in straight lines, so it cannot go around the object. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: When an object blocks light, it makes a shadow.
tips: Opaque objects block light and make dark shadows.

similar_questions.stem: Which material lets almost all light pass through it?
explanation_steps: Clear glass is transparent; light passes through it.

questions.stem: The speed of sound in air is about 330 m/s. How far does it travel in 5 seconds?
explanation_steps: Distance = speed × time = 330 m/s × 5 s = 1650 m.
The options print the unit 'm/s', but a distance is measured in metres (m). The number 1650 is still option B. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 208)
questions.explain_simple: 330 × 5 = 1650. Sound goes 1650 metres in 5 seconds.
tips: distance = speed × time. Distance unit: m, not m/s.

similar_questions.stem: Sound travels at 330 m/s. How long does it take to travel 990 m?
explanation_steps: time = distance ÷ speed = 990 ÷ 330 = 3 s.

questions.review_flag: Misprint: the options give the unit m/s for a distance; they should be in metres (1650 m). Answer B is clear.

questions.stem: In figure 3, structure “X” is:
questions.image_alt: Figure 3: a cut flower. In the middle is a tall part with a round base; a line labelled X points to its stalk. Two thin stalks with small heads are beside it, inside the petals.
explanation_steps: X points to the tall central part with a round base (ovary), a stalk (style) and a top (stigma). This is the pistil.
The pistil is the female part of a flower. The thin parts with heads beside it are stamens (male parts). Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 123)
questions.explain_simple: X is the pistil in the middle of the flower. It is the female part.
tips: Pistil (female) = stigma + style + ovary. Stamen (male) = anther + filament.

similar_questions.stem: Which part of a flower makes pollen?
explanation_steps: Pollen is made in the anther, the top of the stamen.

questions.stem: Change in an organism’s environment is detected by:
explanation_steps: A change in the environment (a stimulus) is detected by receptors.
Receptors send the message to a coordinator; then an effector makes the response. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 84)
questions.explain_simple: Receptors notice changes around us.
tips: Receptor detects → coordinator decides → effector acts.

similar_questions.stem: The eye is a receptor for
explanation_steps: The eye detects light.

questions.stem: A force pushes a box of mass 2 kg to accelerate it by 5 m/s². The box moves a distance of 3 m. The work done by the force is:
explanation_steps: First find the force: F = mass × acceleration = 2 kg × 5 m/s² = 10 N.
Then work = force × distance = 10 N × 3 m = 30 J. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 61; Science Grade 7, p. 59)
tips: Two steps: F = m × a, then W = F × s.

similar_questions.stem: A 4 kg cart accelerates at 2 m/s². What net force acts on it?

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
explanation_steps: A chemical change makes new substances.
Burning paper makes ash, smoke and gases. These are new substances.
Cutting, melting and freezing only change size or state. They are physical changes. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 47)
questions.explain_simple: Burning makes new substances, so it is a chemical change.
tips: New substance → chemical change. Only shape/state changes → physical change.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a physical change?
explanation_steps: Dissolving sugar makes no new substance; you can get the sugar back.

questions.stem: Figure 4 is a model of respiratory system. Structure “C” represents:
questions.image_alt: Figure 4: bell-jar model. A tube goes through a stopper into the jar and branches into two balloons. Label A points to the jar wall, B to the tube, C to the balloons, D to the rubber sheet at the bottom.
explanation_steps: In the bell-jar model, the glass tube is the trachea, the two branches are the bronchi, the balloons are the lungs, and the rubber sheet at the bottom is the diaphragm.
C points to the balloons, so C represents the lungs. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 14; Science Grade 8, p. 12)
questions.explain_simple: C points to the balloons. The balloons are the lungs.
tips: Bell-jar model: jar = chest cavity, tube = trachea, balloons = lungs, rubber sheet = diaphragm.

similar_questions.stem: In the bell-jar model, when the rubber sheet is pulled down, the balloons
explanation_steps: Pulling the sheet down is like breathing in; the balloons (lungs) fill with air.

questions.stem: Meter per second is the SI unit of:
explanation_steps: Velocity is displacement ÷ time, so its unit is metre per second (m/s).
Acceleration is in m/s²; displacement and distance are in metres. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 56)
questions.explain_simple: Velocity is measured in metres per second.
tips: m → distance/displacement; m/s → speed/velocity; m/s² → acceleration.

similar_questions.stem: The SI unit of acceleration is
explanation_steps: Acceleration is change in velocity per second: m/s².

questions.stem: The ratio of atoms in H₂SO₄ is:
explanation_steps: The small number after a symbol tells how many atoms of that element there are. No number means 1.
H₂ = 2 hydrogen, S = 1 sulphur, O₄ = 4 oxygen. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 86)
questions.explain_simple: H₂SO₄ has 2 H, 1 S and 4 O.
tips: No small number = 1 atom.

similar_questions.stem: How many oxygen atoms are in CO₂?
explanation_steps: The small 2 after O means 2 oxygen atoms.

questions.stem: A word equation is given as Carbon + Oxygen → Carbon dioxide. Its equivalent chemical equation is:
explanation_steps: Carbon is written C. Oxygen gas is written O₂ (two atoms). Carbon dioxide is CO₂ (one carbon, two oxygens: 'di' = two).
So the equation is C + O₂ → CO₂. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 90)
questions.explain_simple: Carbon is C, oxygen is O₂ and carbon dioxide is CO₂.
tips: 'di' means two: carbon dioxide = CO₂.

similar_questions.stem: Which is the formula of carbon monoxide?
explanation_steps: 'mono' means one: one carbon and one oxygen = CO.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Chemical Reactions and the Periodic Table

questions.stem: The process of changing water vapour to liquid is called:
explanation_steps: When water vapour cools, it turns into liquid water. This is condensation.
Evaporation is liquid → vapour; solidification is liquid → solid; precipitation is rain falling. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 170)
questions.explain_simple: Vapour turning into liquid is condensation.
tips: Evaporation: liquid → gas. Condensation: gas → liquid.

similar_questions.stem: Wet clothes dry in the sun because of
explanation_steps: The water in the clothes changes into vapour: evaporation.

questions.stem: The cell organelle used for getting energy from food is:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Mitochondrion – is used for getting energy from food.'
Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: The mitochondrion gets energy from food.
tips: Mitochondrion = the 'power house' of the cell.

similar_questions.stem: Which part of a plant cell stores water and cell sap?
explanation_steps: The large vacuole stores water and cell sap.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not the source of fresh water in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Sea water is salty, so it is not fresh water.
Dams, springs and rivers give fresh water. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 166; Science Grade 8, p. 167)
questions.explain_simple: The sea is salty. It is not fresh water.
tips: Fresh water: rivers, dams, springs, wells. Salty water: sea, ocean.

similar_questions.stem: About how much of the earth's water is salty?
explanation_steps: Over 97% of the earth's water is salty sea water.

questions.stem: A secretion which does not contain enzyme for digestion is:
explanation_steps: The textbook says bile does not contain any enzyme for digestion. It has salts that break fat into small drops.
Gastric, pancreatic and intestinal juices all contain enzymes. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Bile has no enzymes. It helps break fat into small drops.
tips: Bile: made in the liver, stored in the gall bladder, no enzyme.

similar_questions.stem: Where is bile made?
explanation_steps: Bile is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder.

questions.stem: Dusting pollen from stamen of a short plant to stigma of a tall plant by hand is:
explanation_steps: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from a stamen (anther) to a stigma.
Here people do it by hand, so it is artificial pollination. (It is between two different plants, so it is not self pollination.)
Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 205)
questions.explain_simple: Moving pollen by hand is artificial pollination.
tips: Pollination by people = artificial pollination; by wind or insects = natural pollination.

similar_questions.stem: Pollen moves from the anther to the stigma of the same flower. This is
explanation_steps: Pollination within the same flower (or plant) is self pollination.

questions.stem: Farmers want to control rats and mice in their farm. The pesticide you would advice them to use is:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Rodenticides are used to control rats and mice.'
Fungicides kill fungi, herbicides kill weeds, insecticides kill insects. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Rodenticides kill rats and mice.
tips: Rodents = rats and mice → rodenticides.

similar_questions.stem: Which pesticide kills insects?
explanation_steps: Insecticides kill insects.
